task.description:
Implement ISS-401..404 on branch feature/WF02-iss401-404-epic4-20260612. Follow design docs exactly.

ISS-401 (src/api/middleware/rate_limit.zig, src/config/*):
- Sliding-window rate limiter middleware using PostgreSQL (BPM_RATE_LIMIT_BACKEND=postgres)
- Table: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rate_limit_buckets (key TEXT, window_start BIGINT, count INT, PRIMARY KEY(key, window_start))
- Logic: on each request, prune old windows; count current window; if over limit → 429 + Retry-After
- Config: BPM_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RPM, BPM_RATE_LIMIT_BACKEND validated at startup
- Key = concat(tenant_id, ':', principal)

ISS-402 (src/oidc/jwks.zig, src/api/middleware/auth.zig):
- OIDC token validation: fetch JWKS from issuer, verify signature, extract claims
- Cache valid tokens in LRU keyed by (realm, jti) with TTL = min(exp - now, 5min)
- Revocation: jti denylist (std.StringHashMap with timestamp), entries expire after token.exp
- On realm logout: add all active jti for that realm to denylist

ISS-403 (src/api/middleware/rate_limit.zig):
- After OIDC auth succeeds: principal = concat(realm, ':', sub)
- After local token auth: principal = api_token.id (as string)
- Rate-limit key = concat(tenant_id, ':', principal)

ISS-404 (src/identity/service.zig):
- Token issuance: copy user_roles into api_tokens.roles[] at creation time
- Token validation: read roles from api_tokens.roles[] (token snapshot), never from user_roles
- Document: changing user_roles does not retroactively alter issued tokens
- Test: issue token, change user_roles, verify token roles unchanged

Run: zig build (exit 0), zig build test (exit 0), zig build 2>&1 | grep -i 'error set' (must be empty).
No I/O in transition.zig. No SQL string interpolation. Commit and push.
acceptance_criteria: ISS-401: rate limiter middleware, sliding window in postgres, 429+Retry-After, config validation
ISS-402: OIDC JWKS validation, (realm,jti) cache, jti denylist, realm logout revocation
ISS-403: OIDC principal rate-limit keying integrated with ISS-401/402
ISS-404: token roles snapshot at issuance, validation reads from token not user_roles
